report:
## PR #2026 — enforce workpad size limits before a write (issue #2024)

**Verdict: APPROVE with notes.** The change adds two fail-closed size guards to `scripts/workpad.py` and is correct on every reviewed path. No Critical or Important findings across all five Phase-3 reviewers; the remaining items are non-blocking Suggestions.

### What was verified correct
- **Per-note budget** (`_check_note_within_budget`, scripts/workpad.py:353) uses `n > 2048` — 2048 accepted / 2049 refused. Runs in `_cmd_update_inner` (scripts/workpad.py:3584) over `_own_notes` only, BEFORE `_plan_buffer_replay`, so buffer-replayed and tool-composed rows are exempt (AC6/AC7) and the permanent-wedge bug this PR fixes is not reintroduced.
- **Comment-body cap** (`_check_body_within_limit`, scripts/workpad.py:370) uses `nbytes > 65536` — 65536 accepted / 65537 refused. Enforced before the PATCH in `_cmd_update_inner` (scripts/workpad.py:3643) and in BOTH branches of `_patch_comment_body` (in-memory `_byte_len(text)` at :1277, file `stat().st_size` at :1290), closing the fail-open file-path route (AC10).
- **AC5** — both checks precede the sole `_buffer_failed_change` call (:3685, inside the PATCH-failure except), so a size refusal buffers nothing; proven by placement and by the monkeypatched-buffer test asserting 0 calls.
- **UTF-8 byte measurement** on both sides (AC11), exit-1 with messages naming the count + limit, `except _UpdateError` ordered before the transport except in `cmd_patch` (no cause masking).
- Tests AC1-AC11 + workpad-cli S1-S3 drive the real guarded paths; assertion floor bumped 94->102 in lockstep in lib/test/run.sh and scripts/workflow-flight-recorder-registry.json; coverage-map maps 2024->workpad-cli. Prompt-prose ACs (one --note per search/comparand) satisfied in both skills/implement files.

### Non-blocking Suggestions (see phase3_findings)
Comment-discipline trims, a stat/UTF-8 phrasing overclaim, an uncoupled `2048` literal mirrored in prose, two partly-tautological/absent test-boundary assertions, and two residual edge cases (pre-existing over-cap buffer cannot drain; lone-surrogate encode traceback) — each fails closed and none blocks merge.

phase3_findings.description: scripts/workpad.py:290 (_patch_comment_body body_path branch) — stat().st_size equals the UTF-8 byte count only if the file is UTF-8; safe (raw bytes are what GitHub receives and st_size is a conservative bound), worth a one-clause note only.

The 2048 budget literal now appears in code (_NOTE_BYTE_BUDGET) and two shipped prose surfaces (phase-2-implement.md, sweep-2-3-0c-operand-trace.md) with nothing pinning them together — coupled sites a future budget change must sweep.

scripts/workpad.py:3643 — a pre-existing failed-write buffer whose folded content exceeds the comment cap re-hits the cap on every update and never reaches the buffer-clear at :3703, so it cannot drain. Not a regression (uncap-able at GitHub too) and out of the issue's scope, but a residual wedge the body-cap exemption does not close.

scripts/workpad.py:350 — _byte_len raises uncaught UnicodeEncodeError on lone-surrogate strings (not an _UpdateError), producing a raw traceback rather than a workpad-framed message. Still fails closed (non-zero exit, no PATCH); extremely unlikely for real workpad text.

scripts/workpad.py:277 — inline comment '# Comment-size limit (issue #2024): measure the in-memory text.' restates the line below it and names no wrong change it prevents; the paired else-branch comment already carries the real warning. Delete per CLAUDE.md comment discipline.

scripts/workpad.py:299-300 — comment half-restates the report+exit lines below; only the 'not a transport error' clause distinguishing it from the following except is load-bearing. Trim to that clause.

scripts/workpad.py:348-349 (_byte_len docstring) and :354-360 (_check_note_within_budget docstring) — design narrative ('The one measurement both size guards use...'; 'Mirrors the sibling _is_single_line guards' convention', an inaccurate attribution since 'No PATCH was made.' is a repo-wide _UpdateError convention). Trim to spec sentences.

scripts/workpad.py:289 — 'Its on-disk byte size is the UTF-8 count' overclaims; st_size is the raw byte count regardless of encoding (equals UTF-8 only if the file is UTF-8). Reword to 'the byte count GitHub receives'.

lib/test/test_python_scripts.py:160-162 (AC4) is driven with patch_fails=True, so its 'exits non-zero'/'no PATCH' assertions are partial tautologies — they pass even if _check_body_within_limit were removed. Only the message and AC5 buffer-count assertions flip. The independent proof comes from workpad-cli.sh S3 (real subprocess, no forced failure), so the guard IS covered, but the py-side AC4 exit/no-PATCH pair is not self-sufficient.

No test that a body of exactly 65536 bytes on the cmd_update route is accepted; the exact-limit acceptance boundary is exercised only on the _patch_comment_body route (test_python_scripts.py:241-245). An off-by-one flipped to '>=' in the update path would not be caught. Shared _COMMENT_BYTE_LIMIT mitigates.

Body-cap refusal message assertions (AC4/S3) check only the limit literal ('65536') and the phrase 'byte count', not that the measured body byte count is rendered — unlike AC1/S1 which assert the measured '2049 bytes'. AC4 says the message 'names byte count'; assertions would pass even if the measured number were dropped.

scripts/workpad.py:3893 — body-cap message calls GitHub's limit a '65536-byte comment limit', but GitHub's actual limit is 65,536 characters (enforced here over bytes as a conservative pre-check). The message does clarify 'the reported count is a byte count', so AC4 is satisfied; purely cosmetic.
